correctness.rationale: Strict positive invariance follows from gamma<=1 and alpha*y0<1. Predator monotonic decay follows from q<1 or divergent harmonic comparison at alpha=gamma using x_n<=x0+rn. A crossing barrier proves x_n diverges; monotone scalar comparison yields x_n=O(log n), which makes predation negligible relative to re*x*exp(-x). Exact time change G(x)=integral dt/f(t) then gives e^{x_n}/(re*x_n*n)->1 and the three-term prey law. Cesaro and harmonic sums give the two distinct predator clocks. No finite simulation replaces this argument.

value.rationale: The paper identifies alpha=gamma as the exact boundary for a positive coexistence fixed point, but absence of coexistence need not determine long-run fate. This theorem completely determines the physically positive noncoexistence dynamics for a natural invariant region and quantifies an unusual universal prey escape law and a genuine exponential-to-subexponential predator clock transition at the border. The precise log-log term and critical n/log n rate are needed for quantitative long-horizon predictions; this is more than a local stability deduction.
